subject: RANGE-1
reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): not passed; opus 8/10, sol 10/10; 1 finding(s) stand, 0 note(s).

items.reason: AC5 says the range stays that of the whole selection when the sort changes. TC-16 uses /?brand=1, but Daybird's page 1 (first 9 by name) already contains its cheapest ($49.99 LumenHead Headlamp) and dearest ($449.99 Blizzard Snowboard) products. The 10th, Wanderer at $109.99, is on page 2. catalog-sort.js only reorders the existing cards on the current page, so the visible set and its min/max never change. The 'Why' claim that the page's own cheapest and dearest change is false. A range derived from the visible page would pass this case. Fix: open / (no filter), choose 'Price: High to Low', and expect the first card to show $249.99, '101 products' and 'Prices $21.99 – $699.00'. items.title: Moving to page 2 keeps the range of the whole selection
covers: AC5: page change keeps the range of the whole selection
AC2: across every page of results
items.reason: AC5 and AC2 require the range to cover every page. Page 2 of the unfiltered catalog holds neither the cheapest nor the dearest product of page 1, so a range computed from the visible page would change here.

items.title: Changing the sort order keeps the range of the whole selection
covers: AC5: sort change keeps the range of the whole selection
items.reason: AC5 requires the range to stay that of the whole selection when the sort changes. The sort runs on the client and only reorders the cards of the current page, so the unfiltered catalog is used: its page 1 spans only $79.99 – $249.99, while the whole selection spans $21.99 – $699.00. A range taken from the visible cards would show the narrower range and fail this case. Brand Daybird and type Navigation cannot discriminate here because their page 1 already holds their cheapest and dearest products. It is e2e because the sort only exists in the browser.

items.title: Repeated type parameters return the range of the union of those types
covers: AC6: optional repeated type parameter
items.reason: AC6 states `type` may be repeated, and TC-RANGE-1-05 only exercises repeated `brand`; the type filter is bound separately, so it needs its own case. Climbing and Navigation are chosen so the lowest price comes from one type and the highest from the other: a range built from only the first type (Climbing, $21.99 – $189.99) or only the last (Navigation, $59.99 – $299.00) fails, and the union's maximum ($299.00) differs from the unfiltered $699.00, so an ignored filter fails too. Functional is the cheapest layer that reaches the real query against the seeded catalog.
